properties.otherAdvice:
The Royal National Park is expected to be busy over the Christmas and New Year holiday period between 21 Dec and 3 Feb.

Visitors are encouraged to check the Royal National Park local alerts before travelling for updates on precinct access.

Walking trails may also be closed due to total fire bans and/or risks, so plan ahead. 

Roads or carparks may close within the Royal National Park when they reach capacity.

The following locations may be affected:

  • Wattamolla Beach carpark
  • Bonnie Vale day use area
  • Audley Valley
  • Wattamolla Rd between Sir Bertram Stevens Dr and Wattamolla Beach carpark
  • Maianbar Rd between Bundeena Dr and Maianbar township
  • Bundeena Dr between Sir Bertram Stevens Dr and Bundeena township

Garie Road is closed between Sir Bertram Stevens Drive and Garie Beach - Garie Road long term closure.

Luke Combs – Live in Australia 2025 at Accor Stadium in Sydney Olympic Park on Friday 31 January and Saturday 1 February. Support act from 6pm, Luke Combs on stage from 8.45pm and finish around 10.45pm each concert night.

With more than 160,000 fans epected over both concert nights, significant traffic delays are expected on roads approaching the precinct and entering car parks, particularly during Friday’s evening peak travel times.  

Motorists should allow plenty of extra travel time on roads approaching Olympic Park including on the M4 Mwy, Homebush Bay Dr, Concord Rd, Lane Cove Rd, Parramatta Rd, Centenary Dr and Silverwater Rd.

  • CAR PARKS: parking in the precinct is in high demand and expected to sell out before the event. Ticketholders who have to drive must pre-book parking ahead of time to secure a space.
  • If you have pre-booked your parking, follow the directions of staff and have your parking ticket ready to show at the car park entry.
  • Alternatively, consider parking at a nearby train station commuter car park and continuing your trip by train to Olympic Park, at no extra cost.

Sydney Olympic Park Authority will close local roads in the precinct to ensure pedestrian safety during events and accommodate additional transport services. For road closure details, view the interactive map.

Thousands of participants are expected to take part in the annual Sun Run event. The 7km run starts at 6:30am and the 10km run starts at 7.15am, both from The Strand in Dee Why with both events finishing at Manly Beach by 10am.

Road closures, parking restrictions and changed traffic conditions will be in effect starting at 3:30am. All roads will reopen by 11am. 

Residents along the course are urged to plan ahead and relocate their vehicles outside the road closure footprint if vehicle access is required on event day. There will be limited vehicle movements permitted while the event is underway. 

ROAD CLOSURES

  • Dee Why – from 3:30am to 9am: sections of Howard Ave, The Strand and Dee Why Pde, The Oaks Ave westbound crossover will be maintained at The Strand until 6am.
  • Dee Why – from 5:15am to 9am: sections of Oaks Ave, Pacific Pde, The Stand, Boronia St, Griffin Rd and Monash Pde will be closed.
  • North Curl Curl to Freshwater – from 5:30am to 9am: sections of Abbott Rd, Griffin Rd, Headland Rd, Pitt Rd, Adams St, Carrington Pde, Charles St, Evans St and surrounding local roads will be closed. Crossover points will be maintained on Pacific Pde at Griffin Rd, Playfair Rd at Pitt Rd, Ross St at Pitt Rd and Headland Rd at Griffin Rd until 6:15am.
  • Freshwater to Queenscliff – from 5:30am to 10am: sections of Lumsdaine Dr, Undercliff Rd, Dalley St, Dowling St, Greycliffe St, Queenscliff Rd and surrounding local roads will be closed. Managed westbound exit on Crown Rd between Dowling St and Cavill St from 5:30am to 6:30am and from 9:15am to 10am.
  • Manly – from 5:30am to 10am: sections of Bridge Rd, Cameron Ave and Collingwood St will be closed.
  • Manly – from 3:30am to 9:30am: sections of North Steyne, Raglan St, Collingwood St and other local roads will be closed.
  • Manly – from 3:30am to 11am: sections of South Steyne, Wentworth St, Ashburner St and Victoria Pde will be closed.

Special event clearway parking restrictions will be in effect from 3am until 9am on roads along the course through Dee Why, North Curl Curl, Freshwater, Queenscliff and Manly, including on sections of Abbott Rd, Howard Ave, The Strand, Evans St, Crown Rd North Steyne and South Steyne.

Clearways are strict no-parking zones for all vehicle types and apply even to local residents and TfNSW Mobility Scheme Permit holders. Check signs carefully as vehicles left in clearways will be towed and a fee applies. If your vehicle is towed, you can search your vehicle registration at the Find My Car website to find its new location, or alternatively call 132 701 to speak to an operator.

The free "Gong Shuttle" bus (routes 55A and 55C) runs every 10 minutes in a loop around Wollongong making stops at North Wollongong Station, Fairy Meadow Station, Gywneville and Wollongong University and Innovation Campus. 

Gong Shuttle buses will run every 10 minutes from 7am until 10pm on Australia Day. The closest stops to the celebrations at Belmore Basin are along Corrimal St and Burelli St.

Due to road closures, the Free Shuttle Bus will travel along Corrimal Street instead of Cliff Road.

From 8pm until 10pm buses that usually run along Crown St and Burelli St will terminate and depart at Burelli St (west of Corrimal St).
properties.otherAdvice:
The Australia Day Aquathon will once again take place along the Wollongong foreshore, with events running from 8am to 12pm. Wollongong's Australia Day event will then start at 4pm and conclude with fireworks at 10pm.


The following roads will be closed from 6am-12pm:

  • Cliff Road, between Harbour Street and Georges Place
  • Elliotts Road, between Squires Way and Fairy Meadow Beach Carpark

The following road closures will be in place from 4pm until 10pm:

  • Cliff Rd between Marine Dr and Georges Pl
  • Harbour St between Market St and Cliff Rd
  • Hector St
  • Hinton St
  • Campbell St from Corrimal St to Wilson St
  • Wilson St
  • Smith St between Corrimal St and Harbour St
  • Market Pl
  • Endeavour Dr will be become one way from 4pm to 8pm

The following road closures will be in place from 8pm until 10pm:

  • Marine Dr
  • Endeavour Dr
  • Crown St from Harbour St to Marine Dr

Managed access will be available for residents during the event.

Motorists should plan ahead as parking and roads can get busy on New Years Eve. The Innovation Campus car park off Squires Way can be used as a park and ride option by using the Free Gong Shuttle Bus.

properties.publicTransport: Ferries will be affected during the day and night due to exclusion zones on the harbour. Buses will also be diverting and using different stops due to road closures. Light rail will not run between Circular Quay and Town Hall from 7.30pm to 10.30pm. Visit transportnsw.info for details.
properties.otherAdvice:
Roads around Circular Quay and The Rocks, and in Milsons Point will close during the day and evening for Australia Day events in the city and around the harbour.

Warringah Freeway upgrade works continue over the Australia Day long weekend, including southbound lane and ramp closures on Sunday 26 January. Allow extra travel time if you are driving from the north. See the entry for the latest updates on traffic changes.

Key road closure timings:

  • 4am to midnight: George St from Essex St to Hickson Rd, and sections of OPT Elevated Rd from Hickson Rd, Circular Quay West, Essex St and Pitt St.
  • 4am to 10:30pm: Sections of Argyle St and Harrington St.
  • 7am to 10am: Hickson Rd from Napoleon St to Pottinger St, Towns Pl from Dalgety Rd to Hickson Rd and Barton St (for Oz Day 10K wheelchair race).
  • 7am to midnight: Hickson Rd from George St to Pottinger St.
  • 6:30pm to 10:30pm: Sections of Macquarie St.
  • 7:30pm to 10:30pm: Cahill Expressway lanes 7 & 8 and Overpass at Circular Quay including the High St, Mount St and Domain Tunnel on-ramps and lane 4 on the Harbour Bridge. Roads in Circular Quay north of Bridge St including sections of Albert St, Alfred St, Circular Quay East, Conservatorium Rd, Dalley St, Essex St, George St, Loftus St, Pitt St, Philip St, Macquarie St, Reiby Place, Underwood St and Young St. 
  • 9:15pm to 10:15pm: Sections of Grosvenor St/Bridge St.
  • 9:15pm to 10:30pm: Sections of Argyle St and Harrington St.
  • The speed limit on the Harbour Bridge will be reduced to 40km/h from 7:30pm to 10.30pm.
  • The Cahill Expressway Circular Quay overpass walkway will be closed from 5pm to 9:30pm. The Sydney Harbour Bridge Walkway and Cycleway will remain open.
  • Milsons Point/Kirribilli 10:30am to 1pm: Olympic Drive between Broughton St and Alfred St South.
  • 7.30pm to 10.30pm: Lane 4 on the Harbour Bridge, Cahill Expressway lanes 7 and 8 and the Circular Quay Overpass will close. High St and Mount St on-ramps from North Sydney and Kirribilli will also be closed.

Special event clearways will be in effect on various roads in Circular Quay and The Rocks from 3am until midnight and throughout the CBD from 5pm until 10.30pm.

Clearways are strict no-parking zones for all vehicle types, and apply even to local residents and TfNSW Mobility Scheme Permit holders. Check signs carefully as vehicles left in clearways will be towed and a fee applies. If your vehicle is towed, you can search your vehicle registration at the Find My Car website to find its new location, or alternatively call 132 701 to speak to an operator.

Pregnancy, Babies & Children’s Expo at Sydney Showground on Saturday and Sunday from 10am to 4pm daily.

Sydney Olympic Park will be very busy on Saturday with 80,000 fans at the Luke Combs concert at nearby Accor Stadium.

Significant traffic delays are expected so motorists should allow plenty of extra travel time on roads approaching Olympic Park including the M4 Mwy, Homebush Bay Dr, Concord Rd, Lane Cove Rd, Parramatta Rd, Centenary Dr and Silverwater Rd.

Roads within the park will be closed so allow extra travel time for Saturday's expo.

  • CAR PARKS: parking in the precinct is in high demand and expected to sell out before the event. Ticketholders who have to drive must pre-book parking ahead of time to secure a space.
  • If you have pre-booked your parking, follow the directions of staff and have your parking ticket ready to show at the car park entry.
  • Alternatively, consider parking at a nearby train station commuter carpark and continuing your trip by train to Olympic Park. You'll need to use an Opal card or contactless payment card/device when travelling on public transport.

Sydney Olympic Park Authority will close local roads in the precinct to ensure pedestrian safety during events and accommodate additional transport services. For road closure details, view the interactive map.
